purpose: Identify missing operations, not solve or score the questions. Selection was fixed before the earlier interrupted run opened the images; this continuation reread the same inputs without replacing them.

cases.requestedOperation: Infer incidence angle from incident and reflected direction vectors.
cases.existingSupport: Plane-mirror reflection is already traced, but the result contract exposes counts rather than incident/reflected direction or incidence-angle inference.
cases.qualification: A scale or arbitrary emitter position would only be needed for an illustrative scene, not for the mathematical angle question. Do not classify the angle as unknowable because those positions are absent.

cases.requestedOperation: Count images in an equilateral enclosure formed by three plane mirrors.
cases.existingSupport: Plane-mirror primitives exist, but the current nonintersecting-surface contract rejects their common endpoints and native interaction counts are not image counts.
cases.qualification: A bounded ray run cannot establish the complete repeated-image count. Do not introduce gaps at the corners and call the enclosure faithful.

cases.requestedOperation: Determine concave-mirror image height and orientation from object height and distance expressed relative to focal length.
cases.existingSupport: No curved mirror is exposed by the adapter. The ideal-lens model is not a permitted substitute.
cases.qualification: The normalized distance is sufficient for a conditional magnification calculation. A numerical drawing scale and a representative object-point interpretation would require explicit declaration.

cases.requestedOperation: Describe the image of an object with prescribed oscillating axial position in front of a concave mirror, including coincidence and magnification conditions.
cases.existingSupport: The new sweep runner can vary an explicit numerical position list, but cannot supply a curved mirror or derive a symbolic time expression.
cases.qualification: Prescribed motion does not require a mechanics engine. Explicit sampled positions could support a later static sweep once the mirror capability exists; they would not prove the continuous symbolic result.

cases.requestedOperation: Infer an entrance angle that reaches critical incidence at a second planar dielectric interface, and assess decreasing that angle.
cases.existingSupport: No refractive-medium regions or Snell/TIR boundary behavior are exposed in the current component contract.
cases.qualification: Explicit adjacent medium indices and boundary normals are essential. The critical-angle equality needs numerical tolerance and analytical qualification, not an invented finite refracted ray.

cases.requestedOperation: Determine transmitted and reflected branch angles in a stack of dielectric media ending in air.
cases.existingSupport: Planar mirrors cannot replace partially reflecting/refracting material boundaries. The current observations do not identify branch-specific angles.
cases.qualification: The diagram shows reflected and transmitted branches; clarify branch attribution rather than prescribing a route to the native engine. Illustrative layer spacings are not measurements from the diagram.

cases.requestedOperation: Determine paraxial optical power of a spherical refracting surface with two specified refractive indices and curvature radius.
cases.existingSupport: An ideal lens lacks the two-medium curved-interface parameters and the requested surface-power result.
cases.qualification: Parallel construction rays in the diagram are not evidence that a point source at a fabricated large distance is part of the question. A parallel source would help depiction, not replace the surface-power model.

cases.requestedOperation: Locate apparent images of an internal bubble through the flat face of a glass hemisphere whose curved surface is silvered.
cases.existingSupport: Requires material refraction plus a curved reflector and distinct direct/reflected image branches, beyond the current lens/plane-mirror return model.
cases.qualification: A single equivalent lens or moved point source would hide the essential mixed physical processes. Adding one planar boundary will not complete this problem.

cases.requestedOperation: Infer accommodation power range for a simplified eye from near/far points and corneal and eye-lens powers.
cases.existingSupport: The engine has focal-length lens inputs but no accommodation or inverse power result, and contact-component reduction is not an automatic allowed transformation.
cases.qualification: A simplified additive-power eye model must be explicit; arbitrary cornea/lens separation must not be inferred. A numerical forward sweep is not by itself an inverse solution.

cases.requestedOperation: Determine a new objective/eyepiece separation after swapping the lenses while preserving angular magnification.
cases.existingSupport: Two ideal lenses can be represented when geometry and illumination are supplied, but angular instrument magnification and its inverse design constraints are absent.
cases.qualification: Clarify the intended viewing/final-image convention and instrument regime. Existing transverse magnification is not angular magnification; do not insert a convenient object position to force an answer.

selectedDirection.nextPhysicsCandidate: One planar dielectric boundary with explicit media and validated refraction/TIR observations, then composable layers.
selectedDirection.reason: Medium-boundary support recurs in B05-B08 and is foundational for both flat and later curved refraction. B07 and B08 retain additional curved/interface/image-analysis gaps. Curved mirrors are a separate recurring candidate in B03, B04 and B08.
selectedDirection.firstMilestoneBoundary: Verify the pinned native implementation first; specify region membership, index ratios, normals, branch semantics, budgets and boundary cases; add one reusable adapter capability with native/contract/round-trip tests. No new ray tracer or question-specific shortcut.
selectedDirection.samplingCaution: Ten deliberately distributed inputs are not a representative estimate of archive coverage. Repeated categories in this review are design evidence, not an accuracy fraction or automatically solved questions.
